notes: Round 4: merged the original Kaggle dataset with BRISC2025 (a 2025 physician-validated, multi-plane academic dataset) into a combined 10,600-image training set / 2,600-image held-out test set, then continued fine-tuning the full EfficientNetB0 backbone (BatchNorm layers excepted) from round 3's weights at 300x300. Best checkpoint saved at epoch 8 (val_accuracy 0.9934) before the training process was interrupted; evaluated on the combined held-out test set and shipped as final. Glioma recall rose from 0.72 (round 3, single dataset) to 0.89, the largest single improvement across all rounds -- consistent with the earlier diagnosis that training data quality/diversity, not model capacity, was the bottleneck.
